title.zh: 卷八十 列傳第五十 王羲之
title.raw: 卷八十 列傳第五十 王羲之 Volume 80 Biographies 50: Wang Xizhi

sentences.zh: 王羲之

translations.literal: Wang Xizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi.

sentences.zh: 王羲之，字逸少，司徒導之從子也。

translations.literal: Wang Xizhi, courtesy name Yishao, was a nephew of Minister of Education Wang Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi, whose courtesy name was Yishao, was a nephew of Wang Dao, the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 祖正，尚書郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zheng was a Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Zheng had served as a Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父曠，淮南太守。

translations.literal: His father Kuang was Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Kuang was the Administrator of Huainan commandery.

sentences.zh: 元帝之過江也，曠首創其議。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan crossed south of the Yangzi, Kuang first originated that proposal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan crossed to the south, Wang Kuang had been the first to advance the plan.

sentences.zh: 羲之幼訥於言，人未之奇。

translations.literal: In youth Xizhi was awkward in speech; people did not regard him as remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Wang Xizhi was tongue-tied, and no one thought him extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 年十三，嘗謁周顗，顗察而異之。

translations.literal: At thirteen he once visited Zhou Yi; Yi observed him and considered him unusual.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he paid a call on Zhou Yi, who sized him up and saw something uncommon in him.

sentences.zh: 時重牛心炙，坐客未啖，顗先割啖羲之，於是始知名。

translations.literal: At the time ox-heart roast was prized; the seated guests had not yet eaten when Yi first carved and fed Xizhi, and thereby he first became known.
translations.idiomatic: Ox-heart roast was then considered a great delicacy; before the other guests had tasted it, Zhou Yi carved a portion for Wang Xizhi—through that gesture the youth first won a name.

sentences.zh: 及長，辯贍，以骨鯁稱，尤善隸書，為古今之冠，論者稱其筆勢，以為飄若浮雲，矯若驚龍。

translations.literal: When grown, he was eloquent and ample, famed for upright backbone; he was especially skilled in clerical script, crown of ancient and modern; critics called his brush momentum as drifting like floating clouds, vigorous like a startled dragon.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was fluent and well spoken, praised for moral backbone, and above all a master of clerical script—the finest of his age. Connoisseurs described his brushwork as drifting like clouds and startling as a twisting dragon.

sentences.zh: 深為從伯敦、導所器重。

translations.literal: He was deeply regarded by his uncles Dun and Dao.
translations.idiomatic: His uncles Wang Dun and Wang Dao held him in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 時陳留阮裕有重名，為敦主簿。

translations.literal: At the time Ruan Yu of Chenliu had a great reputation and was Chief Clerk to Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yu of Chenliu enjoyed enormous prestige at the time and served as Wang Dun's chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 敦嘗謂羲之曰：「汝是吾家佳子弟，當不減阮主簿。

translations.literal: Dun once said to Xizhi, "You are a fine young man of our house; you ought not fall short of Clerk Ruan."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun once told him, "You are one of the best youths in our clan; you should prove no less capable than Clerk Ruan."

sentences.zh: 」裕亦目羲之與王承、王悅為王氏三少。

translations.literal: Yu also regarded Xizhi together with Wang Cheng and Wang Yue as the three young men of the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yu likewise grouped Wang Xizhi with Wang Cheng and Wang Yue as the three rising stars of the Wang family.

sentences.zh: 時太尉郗鑒使門生求女婿于導，導令就東廂遍觀子弟。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Commandant Xi Jian sent a household student to seek a son-in-law from Dao; Dao had him go to the eastern wing and survey all the young men.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Commandant Xi Jian dispatched a dependent to choose a son-in-law among Wang Dao's nephews, Wang Dao told the man to tour the east wing and look over every candidate.

sentences.zh: 門生歸，謂鑒曰：「王氏諸少並佳，然聞信至，咸自矜持。

translations.literal: The student returned and said to Jian, "The Wang youths are all excellent, yet when word of the messenger arrived they all composed themselves."
translations.idiomatic: The messenger reported back to Xi Jian, "The Wang boys are all impressive, but the moment they heard you had sent someone, each put on a stiff, careful air."

sentences.zh: 惟一人在東床坦腹食，獨若不聞。

translations.literal: Only one man lay on the eastern couch with belly exposed eating, alone as if he had not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Only one stayed on the eastern couch, shirt open, eating as if he had not heard a thing.

sentences.zh: 」鑒曰：「正此佳婿邪！

translations.literal: Jian said, "Just this one is the fine son-in-law!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian said, "That is exactly the son-in-law I want."

sentences.zh: 」訪之，乃羲之也，遂以女妻之。

translations.literal: Inquiring, it was Xizhi; thereby he gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: They identified him as Wang Xizhi, and Xi Jian married his daughter to him.

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，征西將軍庾亮請為參軍，累遷長史。

translations.literal: He began office as Palace Secretary; General Who Guards the West Yu Liang summoned him as aide-de-camp, and he was promoted repeatedly to Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a palace secretary, joined General Who Guards the West Yu Liang's staff as an adviser, and rose step by step to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 亮臨薨，上疏稱羲之清貴有鑒裁。

translations.literal: When Liang faced death he submitted a memorial praising Xizhi as pure and noble with discerning judgment.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Yu Liang forwarded a memorial commending Wang Xizhi's integrity, fastidious taste, and sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 遷甯遠將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Makes Distant Lands Tranquil and Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Distance and governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 羲之既少有美譽，朝廷公卿皆愛其才器，頻召為侍中、吏部尚書，皆不就。

translations.literal: Xizhi since youth had a fine reputation; court dukes and ministers all loved his talent and capacity; repeatedly he was summoned as Palace Attendant and Minister of Personnel, yet all he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi had enjoyed an excellent reputation from his youth, and high officials at court prized his gifts; they summoned him repeatedly for posts such as palace attendant and minister of personnel, but he refused every offer.

sentences.zh: 復授護軍將軍，又推遷不拜。

translations.literal: Again he was appointed General Who Guards the Army, and again he deferred and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the generalship of the Guards was offered him once more, he again demurred and never took up the commission.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史殷浩素雅重之，勸使應命，乃遺羲之書曰：「悠悠者以足下出處足觀政之隆替，如吾等亦謂為然。

translations.literal: Inspector Yang Yin Hao had long esteemed him and urged him to answer the summons; thereby he sent Xizhi a letter saying, "Those who talk loosely suppose your accepting or declining office is enough to show whether government rises or falls; people like us also say it is so.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao, the Yangzhou inspector, had always respected him and pressed him to accept appointment; he wrote Wang Xizhi a letter saying, "Casual observers claim that whether you take office mirrors the health of the state—and we think they are right.

sentences.zh: 至如足下出處，正與隆替對，豈可以一世之存亡，必從足下從容之適？

translations.literal: As for your taking office or not, it directly pairs with rise and fall—how can one generation's survival hang entirely on your leisurely comfort?
translations.idiomatic: Your choice to serve or withdraw stands opposite the dynasty's fortune; surely the fate of an age cannot turn solely on what suits your ease.

sentences.zh: 幸徐求眾心。

translations.literal: Fortunately take slowly seeking the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: You should proceed patiently and win the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 卿不時起，復可以求美政不？

translations.literal: If you do not rise in due time, can you again seek good governance?
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse to step forward now, how will good government ever be achieved?

sentences.zh: 若豁然開懷，當知萬物之情也。

translations.literal: If you open your heart broadly, you ought to know the disposition of all things.
translations.idiomatic: If you set aside reserve and engage wholeheartedly, you will grasp what moves the world.

sentences.zh: 」羲之遂報書曰：「吾素自無廊廟志，直王丞相時果欲內吾，誓不許之，手跡猶存，由來尚矣，不於足下參政而方進退。

translations.literal: " Xizhi then replied with a letter saying, "I have never harbored ambition for court rank; when Chancellor Wang truly wished to draw me inside, I swore I would not permit it—the handwritten pledge still exists—and that resolve has long stood; it is not now, as you take part in government, that I suddenly weigh withdrawal or advance.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xizhi answered: "I have never coveted ministerial office. When Chancellor Wang tried to pull me into court I refused on oath; the note still survives, and that resolve is old—it is not because you entered government that I am only now debating whether to serve.

sentences.zh: 自兒娶女嫁，便懷尚子平之志，數與親知言之，非一日也。

translations.literal: Since my sons married and daughters wed, I have cherished Shang Ziping's intent; repeatedly I have spoken of it to kin and friends—not for one day only.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since my children married off I have nursed Shang Ziping's dream of retiring; I have told friends and family again and again, and not just lately.

sentences.zh: 若蒙驅使，關隴、巴蜀皆所不辭。

translations.literal: If I am dispatched on mission, for Guanlong or Bashu I would not decline.
translations.idiomatic: If the court sends me abroad, I would not shrink from duty even to the Guanlong frontier or the Bashu basin.

sentences.zh: 吾雖無專對之能，直謹守時命，宣國家威德，固當不同於凡使，必令遠近咸知朝廷留心於無外，此所益殊不同居護軍也。

translations.literal: Although I lack special skill in embassies, by strictly obeying the timely command and proclaiming the state's awe-inspiring virtue, it ought indeed to differ from ordinary envoys; surely it would make far and near alike know the court cares for those beyond its borders—the benefit differs altogether from sitting as general of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: I may lack polished embassy manners, yet if I simply obey orders and proclaim imperial dignity, I would still surpass the usual envoy and show every quarter that the throne remembers its outer domains—that good exceeds whatever came from holding the Guards command.

sentences.zh: 漢末使太傅馬日磾慰撫關東，若不以吾輕微，無所為疑，宜及初冬以行，吾惟恭以待命。」

translations.literal: At the end of Han they sent Grand Tutor Ma Midi to console Guandong; if you do not doubt me for being insignificant, it would be fit to set out by early winter; I respectfully await the command."
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Han they dispatched Grand Tutor Ma Midi to pacify the east; unless you despise me as too slight a man, send me out at the beginning of winter—I await your orders respectfully."

sentences.zh: 羲之既拜護軍，又苦求宣城郡，不許，乃以為右軍將軍、會稽內史。

translations.literal: Once Xizhi had accepted general of the Guards, he painfully sought Xuancheng commandery; not permitted, he was therefore made General of the Right Army and interior minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Xizhi took the Guards post he pleaded bitterly for Xuancheng; when that was denied he received instead the posts of General of the Right Army and interior minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 時殷浩與桓溫不協，羲之以國家之安在於內外和，因以與浩書以戒之，浩不從。

translations.literal: At the time Yin Hao and Huan Wen were not harmonious; Xizhi considered the state's safety to lie in harmony inside and out; thereby he wrote Hao a letter to warn him; Hao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao and Huan Wen were at odds; Wang Xizhi believed the realm depended on concord between court and commanders, so he warned Yin Hao in a letter—advice Yin ignored.

sentences.zh: 及浩將北伐，羲之以為必敗，以書止之，言甚切至。

translations.literal: When Hao was about to campaign north, Xizhi believed he would surely fail; with a letter he stopped him, the words extremely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Hao prepared a northern expedition Wang Xizhi foresaw disaster and wrote to dissuade him in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 浩遂行果為姚襄所敗。

translations.literal: Hao thereupon went forward and indeed was defeated by Yao Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao marched anyway and, as predicted, suffered defeat at the hands of Yao Xiang.

sentences.zh: 復圖再舉，又遺浩書曰：

translations.literal: Again planning a second advance, he again sent Hao a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Hao plotted another campaign, Wang Xizhi again wrote him a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 知安西敗喪，公私惋怛，不能須臾去懷，以區區江左，所營綜如此，天下寒心，固以久矣，而加之敗喪，此可熟念。

translations.literal: Learning of the western army's rout, public and private were aggrieved and could not set aside the matter for a moment; with this tiny Jiangzuo what has been managed is thus; all under Heaven are chilled at heart—it has long been so—and adding defeat on defeat deserves mature reflection.
translations.idiomatic: News of General Who Pacifies the West's defeat appalled everyone; grief would not lift for an instant. Our narrow foothold south of the Yangzi has been strained to this point—the empire has despaired for ages—and fresh disaster makes reflection imperative.

sentences.zh: 往事豈復可追，顧思弘將來，令天下寄命有所，自隆中興之業。

translations.literal: Past affairs how again can they be pursued; consider instead enlarging the future, causing all under Heaven to entrust their lives somewhere, thereby advancing the enterprise of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The past cannot be undone; look rather to what lies ahead so that people again have something to live for and the revival may proceed.

sentences.zh: 政以道勝寬和為本，力爭武功，作非所當，因循所長，以固大業，想識其由來也。

translations.literal: Government ought to overcome through the Way, taking leniency and harmony as root; striving for military merit is not what is fitting; following what each excels at to consolidate the great enterprise—I suppose you recognize whence this comes.
translations.idiomatic: Rule should prevail through moral authority grounded in tolerance and peace; leaning on force alone is wrong. Play to existing strengths to secure the larger task—you know the reasoning as well as I.

sentences.zh: 自寇亂以來，處內外之任者，未有深謀遠慮，括囊至計，而疲竭根本，各從所志，竟無一功可論，一事可記，忠言嘉謀棄而莫用，遂令天下將有土崩之勢，何能不痛心悲慨也。

translations.literal: Since the turmoil of invaders, those holding office within and without have lacked deep plans and far-reaching thought, tied-sack ultimate schemes, yet exhausted the root; each followed his whim; in the end not one merit can be discussed, not one deed recorded; loyal words and fine plots were cast aside unused—thereby letting all under Heaven verge on collapse—how can one not ache with sorrow and indignation!
translations.idiomatic: Since the barbarian wars, officials at court and in the provinces have shown neither foresight nor caution—always hoarding schemes yet bleeding the realm dry, each chasing private aims until nothing praiseworthy remains and worthy counsel goes unheard. The empire now teeters toward ruin; the heart breaks with rage.

sentences.zh: 任其事者，豈得辭四海之責！

translations.literal: Those undertaking the task—how can they decline responsibility before the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold power cannot escape answering to the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 追咎往事，亦何所復及，宜更虛己求賢，當與有識共之，不可復令忠允之言常屈於當權。

translations.literal: Blaming past events—again what can be remedied; it is fit instead to humble yourself and seek the worthy, acting with those who have insight; do not again let loyal and candid speech habitually bend before those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Recrimination fixes nothing; humble yourself, recruit wise men, and share the burden—and stop letting blunt honesty bow to faction.

sentences.zh: 今軍破於外，資竭於內，保淮之志非復所及，莫過還保長江，都督將各復舊鎮，自長江以外，羈縻而已。

translations.literal: Now the army is broken outside, resources exhausted inside; the will to hold the Huai is no longer attainable—nothing surpasses falling back to guard the Yangzi; area commanders should each restore old garrisons; south of the Yangzi only loose reins remain.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat abroad has emptied the treasury; we can no longer cling to the Huai line—better withdraw behind the Yangzi, restore each commander to former posts, and beyond the river merely maintain a light touch.

sentences.zh: 任國鈞者，引咎責躬，深自貶降以謝百姓。

translations.literal: Those who bear the state's balance should accept blame, blame themselves, deeply demote themselves to apologize to the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: National leaders must own the fault, impose penance on themselves, and step down far enough to apologize to the common people.

sentences.zh: 更與朝賢思布平政，除其煩苛，省其賦役，與百姓更始。

translations.literal: Further join court worthies in pondering broad and fair government, removing its fussiness and severity, lessening levies and corvée, beginning anew with the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Then join conscientious ministers to widen policy, cut red tape and harsh imposts, lighten taxes and labor, and give the people a fresh start.

sentences.zh: 庶可以允塞群望，救倒懸之急。

translations.literal: Perhaps thereby one may satisfy the multitude's hopes and rescue the urgency of hanging upside down.
translations.idiomatic: Only thus may popular expectation be met and the people saved from their desperate plight.

sentences.zh: 使君起于布衣，任天下之重，尚德之舉，未能事事允稱。

translations.literal: The inspector rose from common cloth, bears the weight of all under Heaven; in promoting virtue matters have not wholly matched.
translations.idiomatic: You began as a commoner yet shoulder the empire; even your esteemed appointments have not always lived up to their promise.

sentences.zh: 當董統之任而敗喪至此，恐闔朝群賢未有與人分其謗者。

translations.literal: Having assumed unified command yet brought ruin to this degree—I fear not one worthy in court will share the blame with others.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with supreme leadership you led us to catastrophe; I doubt any colleague will shoulder part of the reproach for you.

sentences.zh: 今亟修德補闕，廣延群賢，與之分任，尚未知獲濟所期。

translations.literal: Now urgently cultivate virtue and mend shortcomings, broadly extend the multitude of worthies, sharing duty with them—still one does not know whether the hoped relief will be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Repair your virtue without delay, widen your circle of advisers, and divide responsibility—and even then success is uncertain.

sentences.zh: 若猶以前事為未工，故復求之於分外，宇宙雖廣，自容何所！

translations.literal: If still you consider prior deeds insufficient skill and therefore seek again beyond measure—though the cosmos is vast, where will there be room for yourself!
translations.idiomatic: If you decide earlier efforts were too tame and grasp for still more—even the wide world may have no place left for you.

sentences.zh: 知言不必用，或取怨執政，然當情慨所在，正自不能不盡懷極言。

translations.literal: I know speech need not be used, or may incur resentment from those in power; yet where passion lies, naturally one cannot fail to pour out one's utmost words.
translations.idiomatic: I realize frank counsel may win no hearing or only anger the mighty; still, feeling leaves no choice but to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 若必親征，未達此旨，果行者，愚智所不解也。

translations.literal: If you insist on personal campaigning and do not grasp this meaning, should it indeed be carried out, foolish and wise alike will not comprehend it.
translations.idiomatic: Should you insist on leading the army yourself without seeing this point, the march itself will baffle everyone, wise or simple.

sentences.zh: 願復與眾共之。

translations.literal: I wish again to share it with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I hope this may be aired openly among our peers.

sentences.zh: 復被州符，增運千石，征役兼至，皆以軍期，對之喪氣，罔知所厝。

translations.literal: Again receiving provincial dispatch, increasing transport by a thousand shi, conscript labor arriving together—all labeled military deadlines—facing it one's breath fails, knowing nowhere to place oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh orders from the province pile another thousand shi of grain transport on us, every duty stamped urgent as war—one feels only despair, at a loss where to turn.

sentences.zh: 自頃年割剝遺黎，刑徒竟路，殆同秦政，惟未加參夷之刑耳，恐勝廣之憂，無復日矣。

translations.literal: In recent years stripping the surviving common people, punished laborers filling the roads, almost matching Qin government policy, only not yet adding the kin-extermination punishment—I fear the worries of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang will not wait for another day.
translations.idiomatic: For years the remnant population has been fleeced until convicts choke the highways—policy nearly as cruel as the Qin's, short only of wholesale clan executions. I dread a popular explosion may come any morning.

sentences.zh: 又與會稽王箋陳浩不宜北伐，並論時事曰：

translations.literal: Again he wrote the Prince of Kuaiji a note stating Yin Hao ought not campaign north, and discussed the times saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Prince Sima Yu of Kuaiji a memorandum arguing against Yin Hao's northern expedition and commenting on current affairs:

sentences.zh: 古人恥其君不為堯舜，北面之道，豈不願尊其所事，比靈斯往代，況遇千載一時之運？

translations.literal: The ancients shamed a ruler who was not Yao or Shun; facing north to serve—how could one not wish to honor whom one serves, comparing soul with past generations, especially encountering a fortune once in a thousand years?
translations.idiomatic: Our forebears blushed if their lord fell short of Yao or Shun; as loyal ministers we too long to ennoble our sovereign and match earlier ages—above all when fortune seems uniquely ripe.

sentences.zh: 顧智力屈于當年，何得不權輕重而處之也。

translations.literal: Only intelligence and strength were exhausted in that year—how could one fail to weigh light and heavy and settle accordingly?
translations.idiomatic: Yet wit and strength have limits in any reign; one must weigh priorities and choose pragmatically.

sentences.zh: 今雖有可欣之會，內求諸己，而所憂乃重於所欣。

translations.literal: Now although there may be occasions for joy, seeking within oneself, what one worries is heavier than what one rejoices.
translations.idiomatic: Even where cause for cheer appears, inwardly anxiety outweighs satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 《傳》云：「自非聖人，外甯必有內憂。

translations.literal: The Tradition says, "Unless one is a sage, outward calm surely harbors inward worry."
translations.idiomatic: The classics remark that except for sages, outward peace conceals inner peril.

sentences.zh: 」今外不寧，內憂已深。

translations.literal: Now outwardly there is no calm; inward worry is already deep.
translations.idiomatic: Today we lack even outward calm, and inward troubles run deep.

sentences.zh: 古之弘大業者，或不謀於眾，傾國以濟一時功者，亦往往而有之。

translations.literal: Those of antiquity who enlarged great enterprises sometimes did not consult the multitude; those who tilted the state to accomplish timely merit also often existed.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient founders sometimes acted without polling everyone; rulers did gamble the realm on single decisive strokes.

sentences.zh: 誠獨運之明足以邁眾，暫勞之弊終獲永逸者可也。

translations.literal: Truly solo judgment bright enough to surpass the multitude, temporary toil's harm finally obtaining eternal ease—such may do.
translations.idiomatic: That works only when unilateral genius truly outshines the crowd and short-term strain buys lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 求之於今，可得擬議乎！

translations.literal: Seeking it in the present—can one propose a parallel!
translations.idiomatic: Look at our situation now—can anyone honestly claim such conditions hold?

sentences.zh: 夫廟算決勝，必宜審量彼我，萬全而後動。

translations.literal: As for temple calculation deciding victory, one must surely examine measuring enemy and self, acting only after completeness of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: War planning demands cold comparison of strengths; move only when every contingency is covered.

sentences.zh: 功就之日，便當因其眾而即其實。

translations.literal: When merit is accomplished, then ought one rely on the multitude thereby and suit reality.
translations.idiomatic: After victory you may lean on popular strength and consolidate real gains.

sentences.zh: 今功未可期，而遺黎殲盡，萬不餘一。

translations.literal: Now merit cannot be expected, yet surviving common people are slaughtered to exhaustion—not one in ten thousand remains.
translations.idiomatic: Today success is nowhere in sight while civilians are massacred until scarcely one in ten thousand survives.

sentences.zh: 且千里饋糧，自古為難，況今轉運供繼，西輸許洛，北入黃河。

translations.literal: Moreover supplying grain a thousand li has since antiquity been difficult—how much more now turning transport and supplying continuation, west delivering to Xu–Luoyang, north entering the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Feeding armies across a thousand miles has always been hellishly hard—especially now that convoys must run west toward Luoyang and north across the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 雖秦政之弊，未至於此，而十室之憂，便以交至。

translations.literal: Although Qin government's abuses did not reach this, yet the worries of ten households thereby arrive together.
translations.idiomatic: Even Qin tyranny stopped short of this; now every village faces simultaneous ruin.

sentences.zh: 今運無還期，徵求日重，以區區吳越經緯天下十分之九，不亡何待！

translations.literal: Now transport has no date of return, exactions daily heavier—with this tiny Wu–Yue weaving the empire's nine-tenths—not perishing—what awaits!
translations.idiomatic: Carriers never come home, levies swell daily, and this small Wu-Yue patch must supply nine-tenths of the realm—if that is not a recipe for extinction, what is?

sentences.zh: 而不度德量力，不弊不已，此封內所痛心歎悼而莫敢吐誠。

translations.literal: Yet not measuring virtue nor strength, not stopping until exhausted—this within the borders is what wrings the heart and draws sighs yet none dares speak sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Still power ignores its limits and drives until collapse—the whole heartland groans yet no one dares speak openly.

sentences.zh: 往者不可諫，來者猶可追，願殿下更垂三思，解而更張，令殷浩、荀羨還據合肥、廣陵，許昌、譙郡、梁、彭城諸軍皆還保淮，為不可勝之基，鬚根立勢舉，謀之未晚，此實當今策之上者。

translations.literal: What is past cannot be remonstrated; what comes still may be pursued—I wish Your Highness again to ponder thrice, loosen and restring, ordering Yin Hao and Xun Xian to return and hold Hefei and Guangling, Xuchang, Qiao commandery, Liang, Pengcheng armies all to fall back and guard the Huai, laying a foundation that cannot be overcome; waiting until roots are planted and momentum raised—planning is not late—this truly is the best policy of the present.
translations.idiomatic: The past is beyond advice, but the future can still be shaped—please reconsider three times, change course, pull Yin Hao and Xun Xian back to Hefei and Guangling, withdraw Xuchang, Qiao, Liang, and Pengcheng troops behind the Huai, and build an impregnable line; once foundations firm you may strike—not too late. That is today's paramount strategy.

sentences.zh: 若不行此，社稷之憂可計日而待。

translations.literal: If this is not done, worries for altars and grain may be counted by days while awaiting.
translations.idiomatic: Ignore this and the dynasty's doom can be numbered in days.

sentences.zh: 安危之機，易於反掌，考之虛實，著於目前，願運獨斷之明，定之於一朝也。

translations.literal: The pivot of safety and peril turns easier than flipping the palm; examining emptiness and fullness, manifest before the eyes—I wish movement of solitary decisive brightness, settling it in one morning.
translations.idiomatic: Safety and disaster pivot as quickly as turning a hand—the facts lie plain before you; I pray you exercise decisive clarity and settle policy at once.

sentences.zh: 地淺而言深，豈不知其未易。

translations.literal: Ground shallow yet words deep—how could one not know it is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: I am a minor figure presuming to speak weighty truth—I know how risky that is.

sentences.zh: 然古人處閭閻行陣之間，尚或幹時謀國，評裁者不以為譏，況廁大臣末行，豈可默而不言哉！

translations.literal: Yet ancients between lanes and battle lines still sometimes intervened in the age and plotted for the state; critics did not deem it blame—how much more attending the rear rank of great ministers—how can one be silent and not speak!
translations.idiomatic: Yet ancients meddled from marketplace or camp for the nation's sake without shame—how much more may a senior minister speak up?

sentences.zh: 存亡所系，決在行之，不可復持疑後機，不定之於此，後欲悔之，亦無及也。

translations.literal: Survival and perdition hinge on execution; the decision lies in acting—one cannot again harbor doubt afterward; not settling here, afterward wishing to regret—again there is no catching up.
translations.idiomatic: Whether we live or die turns on whether you act; hesitate now and remorse will arrive too late.

sentences.zh: 殿下德冠宇內，以公室輔朝，最可直道行之，致隆當年，而未允物望，受殊遇者所以寤寐長歎，實為殿下惜之。

translations.literal: Your Highness's virtue crowns all within the cosmos; assisting court with ducal house—it is most possible to walk the straight path, bringing loftiness to the present year—yet not satisfying popular expectation—those receiving extraordinary favor therefore toss on their beds with long sighs—truly for Your Highness cherishing it.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue caps the realm and you guide the throne as imperial kin—you could rule straight down the middle and lift the age, yet popular hope remains unsated; even favored ministers lie awake sighing for love of you.

sentences.zh: 國家之慮深矣，常恐伍員之憂不獨在昔，麋鹿之游將不止林藪而已。

translations.literal: The state's worry is deep; always I fear Wu Yuan's worry is not alone in antiquity; deer roaming will not stop at forests and marshes only.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's peril runs deep; Wu Zixu's warning may recur, and court refugees may flee beyond mere woodland.

sentences.zh: 願殿下暫廢虛遠之懷，以救倒懸之急，可謂以亡為存，轉禍為福，則宗廟之慶，四海有賴矣。

translations.literal: I wish Your Highness temporarily to set aside concern for empty distance, thereby to rescue the urgency of hanging upside down—can be called taking extinction for preservation, turning disaster into fortune—then the ancestral temples' blessing, within the four seas there is reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Suspend lofty detachment long enough to save people dangling by their heels—turn extinction into survival and curse into blessing—and the temples will rejoice and the realm will trust you.

sentences.zh: 時東土饑荒，羲之輒開倉振貸。

translations.literal: At the time the eastern lands suffered famine; Xizhi then opened granaries and lent relief.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the east Wang Xizhi opened government granaries for relief loans.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷賦役繁重，吳會憂甚，羲之每上疏爭之，事多見從。

translations.literal: Yet court levies and corvée were heavy; Wu and Guiji suffered extremely; Xizhi repeatedly submitted memorials arguing; matters mostly found acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Court taxes and labor gangs remained crushing—Kuaiji suffered worst—yet Wang Xizhi kept memorializing against abuses and usually won concessions.

sentences.zh: 又遺尚書僕射謝安書曰：

translations.literal: Again he sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Xie An a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Vice Director Xie An:

sentences.zh: 頃所陳論，每蒙允納，所以令下小得蘇息，各安其業。

translations.literal: Recently what I presented and argued—each time received permission—thereby orders below allowed slight restoration of breath; each secured his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposals I have lately laid before you have mostly been approved, so local directives eased slightly and people could tend their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 若不耳，此一郡久以蹈東海矣。

translations.literal: If not thus, this commandery long since would have stumbled into the eastern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Without that indulgence this prefecture would long ago have slid into the ocean—meaning utter ruin.

sentences.zh: 今事之大者未布，漕運是也。

translations.literal: Now among great matters not yet announced, canal transport is it.
translations.idiomatic: Among unfinished business none looms larger than grain transport by water.

sentences.zh: 吾意望朝廷可申下定期，委之所司，勿復催下，但當歲終考其殿最。

translations.literal: My meaning hopes the court may extend downward fixed deadlines, entrust them to responsible offices, do not again urge downward—only at year's end examine best and worst performance.
translations.idiomatic: I urge the court to set firm deadlines, leave execution to the proper bureaus, stop hectored micromanagement, and judge officers solely by year-end performance.

sentences.zh: 長吏尤殿，命檻車送詣天臺。

translations.literal: Prefects especially worst—order caged carts deliver them to the celestial terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The worst magistrates should ride prison wagons to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三縣不舉，二千石必免，或可左降，令在疆塞極難之地。

translations.literal: Three counties not raising revenue—two-thousand-bushel rank surely dismissed—or possibly demoted leftward, ordered to extreme hardship posts on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Fail three districts under your charge and a two-thousand-bushel official must be cashiered—or demoted to some miserable border post.

sentences.zh: 又自吾到此，從事常有四五，兼以台司及都水御史行台文符如雨，倒錯違背，不復可知。

translations.literal: Moreover since I arrived here, attendants constantly four or five, compounded by Secretariat and capital waterworks censor traveling terrace documents like rain—inverted wrong violating—again unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: Since I reached this post four or five aides jostle about while Secretariat, capital hydrology, and touring inspectors shower contradictory orders—nothing lines up.

sentences.zh: 吾又瞑目循常推前，取重者及綱紀，輕者在五曹。

translations.literal: Again I shut eyes following convention pushing forward—taking heavy belong to overseers, light belong to the five bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Closing my eyes I simply follow routine: weighty cases go to senior clerks, light ones to the five departments.

sentences.zh: 主者蒞事，未嘗得十日，吏民趨走，功費萬計。

translations.literal: Those presiding over affairs never obtain ten days; clerks and common people hurry about—merit expense ten thousandfold reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: No chief officer lasts ten days straight; runners and townsfolk dash until wasted effort mounts astronomically.

sentences.zh: 卿方任其重，可徐尋所言。

translations.literal: Sir, you are assuming its weight—may slowly seek what was stated.
translations.idiomatic: You now shoulder that burden—please review what I have said at leisure.

sentences.zh: 江左平日，揚州一良刺史便足統之，況以群才而更不理，正由為法不一，牽制者眾，思簡而易從，便足以保守成業

translations.literal: In Jiangzuo ordinary times, one good Inspector of Yangzhou sufficed to unify it—how much more with a crowd of talents yet again not governed—straight because law was not one, those restraining were many—thinking simple and easy to follow—then sufficient to guard and preserve accomplished enterprise
translations.idiomatic: In normal times south of the Yangzi a single competent Yangzhou inspector could hold everything together—yet now, rich in talent, we still misrule because laws conflict and too many hands tug the reins; simplify procedure so people can comply and we might keep what we have.

sentences.zh: 倉督監耗盜官米，動以萬計，吾謂誅翦一人，其後便斷，而時意不同。

translations.literal: Granary overseers supervising consumed and stole official rice—actions by ten thousand measure—I said executing and pruning one person—afterward then stopped—yet timely intention differed.
translations.idiomatic: Granary clerks embezzle tens of thousands of hu of state grain; I argued executing one ringleader would stop it—but opinion upstairs disagreed.

sentences.zh: 近檢校諸縣，無不皆爾。

translations.literal: Recently inspecting various counties—not one was not thus.
translations.idiomatic: Recent audits show every county guilty of the same.

sentences.zh: 余姚近十萬斛，重斂以資奸吏，令國用空乏，良可歎也。

translations.literal: Yuyao nearly one hundred thousand hu—heavy levies thereby supplying deceitful clerks—orders national use empty exhausted—truly may be sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyao alone sits on nearly one hundred thousand hu while cruel taxes feed corrupt officers—state stocks drain dry; it breaks the heart.

sentences.zh: 自軍興以來，征役及充運死亡叛散不反者眾，虛耗至此，而補代循常，所在凋困，莫知所出。

translations.literal: Since armies rose, conscription labor and filling transport—death desertion scattering not returning—many; hollow exhaustion reaching thus—yet replacement follows convention—everywhere withered exhausted—not knowing what emerges.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, draftees and river crews die, desert, or vanish without return; the treasury is hollow yet replacements continue by rote until districts collapse with no idea how to cope.

sentences.zh: 上命所差，上道多叛，則吏及叛者席捲同去。

translations.literal: Those whom superior orders dispatch—on the road many rebel—then clerks together with rebels roll up alike and depart.
translations.idiomatic: Men drafted by imperial command often desert along the way; then officials and deserters flee together in a rout.

sentences.zh: 又有常制，輒令其家及同伍課捕。

translations.literal: Moreover there is standing regulation: always order their families and fellow five-household units to pursue capture.
translations.idiomatic: Standing rules also make each man's family and his five-household mutual-responsibility group hunt him down.

sentences.zh: 課捕不擒，家及同伍尋復亡叛。

translations.literal: If pursuit capture does not seize them, families and fellow five-household units soon again flee in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When those patrols fail, the families and neighbors soon desert too.

sentences.zh: 百姓流亡，戶口日減，其源在此。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames drift in exile; household registers daily shrink—the source lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners scatter as refugees while the census shrinks daily—and this is why.

sentences.zh: 又有百工醫寺，死亡絕沒，家戶空盡，差代無所，上命不絕，事起成十年、十五年，彈舉獲罪無懈息而無益實事，何以堪之！

translations.literal: Moreover concerning artisans and temple physicians—death cuts off lines—households empty utterly—replacement nowhere—superior orders unceasing—affairs arising ten years, fifteen years—impeachment and punishment for crimes without slackening breath—yet no benefit to real administration—how can one endure it!
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen and temple healers die without heirs until workshops stand empty, yet quotas never stop—cases drag ten or fifteen years of endless accusations that punish clerks without fixing anything. Who can bear it?

sentences.zh: 謂自今諸死罪原輕者及五歲刑，可以充此，其減死者，可長充兵役，五歲者，可充雜工醫寺，皆令移其家以實都邑。

translations.literal: I propose that from now those death sentences originally light and five-year penal labor may fill this; those whose death is commuted may long fill military service; five-year ones may fill miscellaneous labor and temple posts—all ordered to move their households thereby to replenish capital districts.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth commute lighter capital cases and five-year sentences into these roles: spare the rope by drafting convicts into the army, assign five-year men to workshops and temple chores, and relocate their families to swell the capital population.

sentences.zh: 都邑既實，是政之本，又可絕其亡叛。

translations.literal: Capital districts once filled—this is governance's root—again one can cut off their fleeing rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Stocking the metropolis is fundamental policy and stops people from running away.

sentences.zh: 不移其家，逃亡之患復如初耳。

translations.literal: If one does not move their households, the worry of flight returns as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Skip forced relocation and desertion starts all over again.

sentences.zh: 今除罪而充雜役，盡移其家，小人愚迷，或以為重於殺戮，可以絕奸。

translations.literal: Now removing crime by filling miscellaneous labor—utterly moving their households—the petty man foolishly confused—some consider it heavier than execution—thereby can cut off treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing execution with penal labor plus resettlement looks cruel to simple folk—yet it deters crime better than the axe.

sentences.zh: 刑名雖輕，懲肅實重，豈非適時之宜邪！

translations.literal: Though the statutory label is light, deterrence and solemnity are truly heavy—is this not timely fitness!
translations.idiomatic: The sentence sounds mild but bites harder—is that not exactly what the moment needs?

sentences.zh: 羲之雅好服食養性，不樂在京師，初渡浙江，便有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Xizhi by nature loved ingesting elixirs and nurturing life; he did not delight in the capital; the first time he crossed the Zhe River he harbored intent to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi doted on alchemical regimen and quietist longevity; he disliked Luoyang, and once he crossed into Zhedong he resolved to finish his life there.

sentences.zh: 會稽有佳山水，名士多居之，謝安未仕時亦居焉。

translations.literal: Kuaiji had fine hills and waters; famous gentlemen mostly dwelt there—Xie An before taking office also dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji's landscape drew celebrated scholars—Xie An lived there too before he entered government.

sentences.zh: 孫綽、李充、許詢、支遁等皆以文義冠世，並築室東土，與羲之同好。

translations.literal: Sun Chuo, Li Chong, Xu Xun, Zhi Dun and others all with literary doctrine crowned the age; together they built chambers in the eastern lands, sharing Xizhi's tastes.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuo, Li Chong, Xu Xun, Zhi Dun, and their circle led the age in letters; each raised a villa in the east and kept Wang Xizhi company.

sentences.zh: 嘗與同志宴集于會稽山陰之蘭亭，羲之自為之序以申其志，曰：

translations.literal: Once with like-minded men he feasted south of Kuaiji's Mount Kuaiji at the Orchid Pavilion; Xizhi himself composed its preface to declare his intent, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He once joined kindred spirits for a banquet at the Orchid Pavilion south of Shanyin and drafted the famous preface himself; it begins:

sentences.zh: 永和九年，歲在癸丑，暮春之初，會於會稽山陰之蘭亭，修禊事也。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yonghe, the cyclical year guichou, at the opening of late spring, we gathered at the Orchid Pavilion south of Mount Kuaiji in Shanyin, to observe the purification ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: It was the ninth year of Yonghe, the guichou year in the cycle, early in the third month; we met south of Kuaiji Mountain at Shanyin's Orchid Pavilion for the spring ablution rite.

sentences.zh: 群賢畢至，少長咸集。

translations.literal: All worthy guests arrived; young and old alike assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Every eminent visitor came, young men and elders together.

sentences.zh: 此地有崇山峻嶺，茂林修竹，又有清流激湍，映帶左右，引以為流觴曲水，列坐其次。

translations.literal: This place had lofty peaks and steep ridges, lush woods and tall bamboo; again clear currents rushed swift, mirrored and belted left and right—we drew them to form a winding channel for floating cups—and seated in ranks beside it.
translations.idiomatic: Peaks rose sheer, bamboo groves thickened, and bright rapids curled past us on either side; we turned them into a meandering stream for the wine-cup game and sat along its banks.

sentences.zh: 雖無絲竹管弦之盛，一觴一詠，亦足以暢敘幽情。

translations.literal: Although lacking the grandeur of silk and bamboo orchestras, one cup and one poem still sufficed to release pent feelings in full.
translations.idiomatic: Even without full orchestras, each cup paired with a verse was enough to voice the heart's hidden moods.

sentences.zh: 是日也，天朗氣清，惠風和暢，仰觀宇宙之大，俯察品類之盛，所以遊目騁懷，足以極視聽之娛，信可樂也。

translations.literal: On this day the sky was bright and air clear; the mild breeze blew gentle—looking up we surveyed the vastness of heaven and earth; looking down we inspected the abundance of creatures—thereby roaming the eye and freeing the breast—sufficient to exhaust the pleasures of sight and hearing—truly delightful.
translations.idiomatic: That day broke fair and mild; lifting our eyes we took in the cosmos, lowering them the teeming forms of life—enough to wander vision and ease the soul, to glut eye and ear with joy.

sentences.zh: 夫人之相與，俯仰一世，或取諸懷抱，悟言一室之內，或因寄所托，放浪形骸之外。

translations.literal: As for people's dealings with one another—lifting and lowering through one lifetime—some take from what they hold in the breast and converse in quiet within a chamber; some rely on what they entrust themselves to and roam beyond bodily form.
translations.idiomatic: Men move through a single lifetime in countless ways: some pour out private thoughts in sealed rooms; others chase passions abroad and forget the body.

sentences.zh: 雖趣舍萬殊，靜躁不同，當其欣於所遇，暫得於己，快然自足，不知老之將至。

translations.literal: Although inclinations to take or leave differ in myriad ways, stillness and bustle unlike—when each rejoices in what he meets, briefly gains it within himself—swiftly self-sufficient—not knowing old age's approach.
translations.idiomatic: Preferences diverge—some restless, some still—but whenever joy strikes and we clutch that moment, we feel utterly content and forget age stealing on us.

sentences.zh: 及其所之既倦，情隨事遷，感慨系之矣。

translations.literal: When what they pursue wearies, feeling follows circumstance and shifts—sighs attach to it.
translations.idiomatic: When satiation fades, mood swings with changing affairs—and regret follows.

sentences.zh: 向之所欣，俯仰之間，已為陳跡，猶不能不以之興懷。

translations.literal: What once delighted—in the space of a breath—already becomes stale traces—still one cannot fail thereby to stir the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Joy that thrilled us moments ago turns instantly into dusty memory, yet memory still moves us.

sentences.zh: 況修短隨化，終期於盡。

translations.literal: Moreover long and short follow transformation—ultimately they end in exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Life spans long or short obey fate's turning—and every span ends in extinction.

sentences.zh: 古人云，死生亦大矣，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: The ancients said—death and life too are great—is this not painful!
translations.idiomatic: The wise called death and life the greatest of matters—how can we not grieve?

sentences.zh: 每覽昔人興感之由，若合一契，未嘗不臨文嗟悼，不能喻之於懷。

translations.literal: Whenever I read how past men rose to feeling—if matching one tally—I never fail facing the text to sigh in mourning—unable to convey it in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read old laments I feel the author speaks straight to my heart—yet words can never fully carry that ache.

sentences.zh: 固知一死生為虛誕，齊彭殤為妄作，後之視今，亦猶今之視昔，悲夫！

translations.literal: Thus I know treating death and life as one is hollow absurdity; equalizing Pengzu and the dying child is reckless fabrication—those after viewing now—again like those now viewing past—alas!
translations.idiomatic: So I reject Zhuangzi's fantasy that life and death are the same or that long life equals early death; future readers will pity us just as we pity antiquity—what sorrow!

sentences.zh: 故列敘時人，錄其所述，雖世殊事異，所以興懷，其致一也。

translations.literal: Therefore I array narrate contemporaries and record what they composed—although generations differ and affairs change—the means whereby feeling rises—their drift is one.
translations.idiomatic: Here I list today's poets and preserve their verses; ages may change, but the cause of our moods stays one.

sentences.zh: 後之覽者，亦將有感於斯文。

translations.literal: Those who view later—again will have feeling toward this writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later readers will yet respond to these lines.

sentences.zh: 或以潘岳《金穀詩序》方其文，羲之比于石崇，聞而甚喜。

translations.literal: Some compared his text to Pan Yue's preface to the Golden Valley poems—Xizhi likened himself to Shi Chong—hearing it greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Critics paired his prose with Pan Yue's preface to the Golden Valley poems; Wang Xizhi, hearing himself compared to Shi Chong, was delighted.

sentences.zh: 性愛鵝，會稽有孤居姥養一鵝，善鳴，求市未能得，遂攜親友命駕就觀。

translations.literal: By nature he loved geese; Kuaiji had a widow living alone who raised a goose skilled at calling—seeking to buy it he could not obtain it—thereupon with kin and friends he ordered carriages and went to view it.
translations.idiomatic: He adored geese; an old woman in Kuaiji kept a famously vocal bird he tried to buy in vain, so he drove out with friends simply to admire it.

sentences.zh: 姥聞羲之將至，烹以待之，羲之嘆惜彌日。

translations.literal: The old woman heard Xizhi would arrive—cooked it awaiting him—Xizhi sighed in regret a full day.
translations.idiomatic: Learning he was coming she slaughtered the goose for his meal; Wang Xizhi mourned the loss for days.

sentences.zh: 又山陰有一道士，養好鵝，羲之往觀焉，意甚悅，固求市之。

translations.literal: Again in Shanyin there was a Daoist who raised fine geese—Xizhi went to view them—intent greatly pleased—firmly sought to buy them.
translations.idiomatic: In Shanyin a priest kept splendid geese; Wang Xizhi visited, adored them, and pressed to purchase the flock.

sentences.zh: 道士云：「為寫《道德經》，當舉群相贈耳。

translations.literal: The Daoist said, "If you write out the Dao De Jing for me, I will present the whole flock as gift."
translations.idiomatic: The priest said, "Copy the Dao De Jing and the birds are yours."

sentences.zh: 」羲之欣然寫畢，籠鵝而歸，甚以為樂。

translations.literal: Xizhi gladly finished writing—caged the geese and returned—considered it great pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He happily copied the classic, boxed up the geese, and went home overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 其任率如此。

translations.literal: His uninhibited spontaneity was like this.
translations.idiomatic: His heedless candor ran in such veins.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣門生家，見棐幾滑淨，因書之，真草相半。

translations.literal: Once visiting a disciple's home he saw a lacquer table smooth and clean—thereupon wrote on it—true script and cursive half and half.
translations.idiomatic: Calling on a student he found a gleaming lacquer desk and covered half in regular script, half in cursive.

sentences.zh: 後為其父誤刮去之，門生驚懊者累日。

translations.literal: Afterward the student's father mistakenly scraped it away—the disciple startled and mortified many days.
translations.idiomatic: The boy's father later scraped the surface clean; the youth agonized for days.

sentences.zh: 又嘗在蕺山見一老姥，持六角竹扇賣之。

translations.literal: Again once at Mount Ji he saw an old woman holding hexagonal bamboo fans selling them.
translations.idiomatic: Another time on Mount Ji he met an old vendor hawking hexagonal bamboo fans.

sentences.zh: 羲之書其扇，各為五字。

translations.literal: Xizhi wrote on her fans—each five characters.
translations.idiomatic: He inscribed five characters on each fan.

sentences.zh: 姥初有慍色。

translations.literal: The old woman at first had an offended expression.
translations.idiomatic: She scowled at first.

sentences.zh: 因謂姥曰：「但言是王右軍書，以求百錢邪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he told the old woman, "Only say it is General of the Right Army Wang's writing—to seek a hundred cash apiece."
translations.idiomatic: He told her, "Say General of the Right Army Wang brushed these lines and charge a hundred cash each."

sentences.zh: 」姥如其言，人競買之。

translations.literal: The old woman as he said—people competed to buy them.
translations.idiomatic: She did—and buyers mobbed her stall.

sentences.zh: 他日，姥又持扇來，羲之笑而不答。

translations.literal: Another day the old woman again brought fans—Xizhi smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When she returned for another round he only smiled and refused.

sentences.zh: 其書為世所重，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His calligraphy being prized by the generation—all such kinds.
translations.idiomatic: The age prized his brushwork—such tales illustrate why.

sentences.zh: 每自稱「我書比鐘繇，當抗行；

translations.literal: He often called himself, "My script compared to Zhong Yao ought to stand shoulder to shoulder;
translations.idiomatic: He used to boast, "Beside Zhong Yao's regular hand mine should rank equal;

sentences.zh: 比張芝草，猶當雁行也」。

translations.literal: compared to Zhang Zhi's cursive—still ought to trail like wild geese in formation."
translations.idiomatic: against Zhang Zhi's draft script I still fly in his wake like geese in column."

sentences.zh: 曾與人書云：「張芝臨池學書，池水盡黑，使人耽之若是，未必後之也。

translations.literal: Once he wrote someone a letter saying, "Zhang Zhi studied calligraphy beside the pond until the pond water all turned black—if it made men obsess so—perhaps not necessarily behind him.
translations.idiomatic: In one letter he wrote, "Zhang Zhi practiced until his ink darkened an entire pool—devotion so fierce might yet equal his achievement."

sentences.zh: 」羲之書初不勝庾翼、郗愔，及其暮年方妙。

translations.literal: Xizhi's writing at first did not surpass Yu Yi and Xi Yin—reaching his late years then became marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: Early work aside, only in old age did Wang Xizhi eclipse Yu Yi and Xi Yin.

sentences.zh: 嘗以章草答庾亮，而翼深歎伏，因與羲之書云：「吾昔有伯英章草十紙，過江顛狽，遂乃亡失，常歎妙跡永絕。

translations.literal: Once with draft-script cursive he answered Yu Liang—and Yi deeply sighed submission—thereby wrote Xizhi a letter saying, "Formerly I owned ten sheets of Boying draft-script cursive—crossing the Yangzi in desperate confusion—thereupon lost them—always sighed that marvelous traces were forever gone.
translations.idiomatic: When he replied to Yu Liang in draft cursive, Yu Yi marveled and wrote, "I once owned ten pages of Zhang Zhi's grass script but lost them fleeing south—I mourned those masterpieces as gone forever.

sentences.zh: 忽見足下答家兄書，煥若神明，頓還舊觀。」

translations.literal: Suddenly seeing your reply to my elder brother's letter—radiant as spiritual brilliance—instantly restores the old view."
translations.idiomatic: Now your answer to my brother shines like a miracle—my treasure seems restored."

sentences.zh: 時驃騎將軍王述少有名譽，與羲之齊名，而羲之甚輕之，由是情好不協。

translations.literal: At the time General of Agile Cavalry Wang Shu from youth had a fair reputation—with Xizhi equally famed—yet Xizhi greatly slighted him—thereby feelings and friendship did not harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Shu once matched Wang Xizhi in fame, yet Xizhi despised him and they became estranged.

sentences.zh: 述先為會稽，以母喪居郡境，羲之代述，止一吊，遂不重詣。

translations.literal: Shu first served as Kuaiji interior minister—because mother's mourning dwelt within command borders—Xizhi replaced Shu—stopped at one condolence visit—thereupon did not visit again.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu governed Kuaiji while mourning his mother locally; when Wang Xizhi succeeded him he offered a single condolence call and never returned.

sentences.zh: 述每聞角聲，謂羲之當候己，輒灑掃而待之。

translations.literal: Shu whenever hearing horn sounds—thought Xizhi would await himself—always sprinkled water and swept awaiting him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wang Shu heard sedan horns he assumed Xizhi was coming and swept his courtyard in readiness—for years.

sentences.zh: 如此者累年，而羲之竟不顧，述深以為恨。

translations.literal: Thus many years—yet Xizhi ultimately did not attend—Shu deeply took it as resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Years passed and Xizhi never appeared; Wang Shu nursed a bitter grudge.

sentences.zh: 及述為揚州刺史，將就征，周行郡界，而不過羲之，臨發，一別而去。

translations.literal: When Shu became Inspector of Yangzhou—about to answer summons—he toured the command borders—yet did not pass Xizhi—on the verge of departure—one farewell then left.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Yangzhou inspector, Wang Shu toured Kuaiji yet avoided Xizhi until departure day, when he bid one cold farewell.

sentences.zh: 先是，羲之常謂賓友曰：「懷祖正當作尚書耳，投老可得僕射。

translations.literal: Earlier Xizhi often told guests and friends, "Huai ought only become Minister of Education—in old age perhaps attain Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi used to assure guests that Wang Shu might peak as minister of education and perhaps reach vice director in old age.

sentences.zh: 更求會稽，便自邈然。

translations.literal: Further seeking Kuaiji—then himself remote beyond reach."
translations.idiomatic: Expecting him ever to govern Kuaiji as well—that was simply beyond him."

sentences.zh: 」及述蒙顯授，羲之恥為之下，遣使詣朝廷，求分會稽為越州。

translations.literal: When Shu received conspicuous appointment—Xizhi shamed to stand below him—sent agents to court—seeking to divide Kuaiji as Yue Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Wang Shu won high rank Wang Xizhi, mortified to rank beneath him, petitioned to carve Kuaiji into a separate Yue Province.

sentences.zh: 行人失辭，大為時賢所笑。

translations.literal: The envoy missed proper wording—greatly became laughed at by timely worthies.
translations.idiomatic: His messenger bungled the plea and drew ridicule across court.

sentences.zh: 既而內懷愧歎，謂其諸子曰：「吾不減懷祖，而位遇懸邈，當由汝等不及坦之故邪！

translations.literal: Thereupon inwardly harboring shame and sigh—told his various sons, "I am not inferior to Huai—yet position and fortune hang remote—surely because you all do not reach Tan's cause!"
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, he told his sons, "I am Wang Shu's peer in talent yet trail far behind—perhaps because none of you equals Wang Tan."

sentences.zh: 」述後檢察會稽郡，辯其刑政，主者疲于簡對。

translations.literal: Shu afterward inspected Kuaiji command—investigated its punishments and administration—those presiding exhausted answering documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shu later audited Kuaiji, clerks collapsed under his interrogations.

sentences.zh: 羲之深恥之，遂稱病去郡，于父母墓前自誓曰：「維永和十一年三月癸卯朔，九日辛亥，小子羲之敢告二尊之靈。

translations.literal: Xizhi deeply shamed—thereupon claimed illness and left the command—before parents' tombs personally swore, saying, "On guimao new moon of the third month, ninth day xinhai of the eleventh year of Yonghe—your child Xizhi dares announce to the two venerable spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Wang Xizhi resigned on illness and before his parents' graves swore: "Eleventh year of Yonghe, third month, day xinhai—I, Xizhi, declare to Father and Mother:

sentences.zh: 羲之不天，夙遭閔凶，不蒙過庭之訓。

translations.literal: Xizhi lacks Heaven's blessing—early encountered grievous bereavement—not receiving instruction passed across the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: I lacked Heaven's favor—orphaned young—and never heard my father's lessons.

sentences.zh: 母兄鞠育，得漸庶幾，遂因人乏，蒙國寵榮。

translations.literal: Mother and elder brother reared me—attained gradual near-worth—thereupon because others lacked talent—received state's favor and glory.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and elder brother raised me until I somewhat matured; when talent ran thin at court I still won imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 進無忠孝之節，退違推賢之義，每仰詠老氏、周任之誡，常恐死亡無日，憂及宗祀，豈在微身而已！

translations.literal: Advancing lacked loyalty and filial integrity—withdrawing violated yielding worthies' righteousness—whenever looking up chanting Laozi's and Zhou Ren's warnings—always feared death had no day—worry reaching ancestral sacrifices—not only in this slight body!
translations.idiomatic: In office I showed neither loyalty nor piety; in retirement I betrayed the duty to yield to worthies. Laozi and Zhou Ren's warnings haunt me—I dread sudden death and ruin to our line—not merely personal extinction.

sentences.zh: 是用寤寐永歎，若墜深谷。

translations.literal: Therefore waking and sleeping eternal sigh—as if falling into a deep valley.
translations.idiomatic: Sleep brings only sighs—as though I plummeted into a gorge.

sentences.zh: 止足之分，定之於今。

translations.literal: The portion of stopping sufficiency—I settle it today.
translations.idiomatic: Today I fix the limit of knowing when to stop.

sentences.zh: 謹以今月吉辰肆筵設席，稽顙歸誠，告誓先靈。

translations.literal: Respectfully on this month's auspicious morning spread mats and set seats—knocking forehead returning sincerity—announcing oath before prior spirits.
translations.idiomatic: On this auspicious day I spread offerings, strike my brow in homage, and swear before your souls.

sentences.zh: 自今之後，敢渝此心，貪冒苟進，是有無尊之心而不子也。

translations.literal: From today after—daring to violate this heart—greedy adventitious advancement—is having no respect for elders and not being a son.
translations.idiomatic: If hereafter I break this vow for greedy ambition, I dishonor you and cease to be a son.

sentences.zh: 子而不子，天地所不覆載，名教所不得容。

translations.literal: A son yet not a son—Heaven and Earth do not cover or bear—famous teaching cannot contain.
translations.idiomatic: Unfilial sons Heaven and Earth disown—rite cannot shelter them.

sentences.zh: 信誓之誠，有如皦日！」

translations.literal: The sincerity of sworn faith—is like the blazing sun!"
translations.idiomatic: May this oath blaze bright as noon!"

sentences.zh: 羲之既去官，與東土人士盡山水之遊，弋釣為娛。

translations.literal: Once Xizhi left office—with eastern lands gentlemen exhausted hills and waters roaming—archery and fishing for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Out of office he roamed Zhedong's rivers and peaks with local friends, hunting and angling for sport.

sentences.zh: 又與道士許邁共修服食，采藥石不遠千里，遍游東中諸郡，窮諸名山，泛滄海，歎曰：「我卒當以樂死。

translations.literal: Again with Daoist Xu Mai jointly cultivated ingestion—gathering herbs and minerals not shunning a thousand li—everywhere touring eastern interior commands—exhausting famous mountains—floating the deep sea—sighed saying, "I ultimately ought to die of joy.
translations.idiomatic: With the adept Xu Mai he swallowed elixirs and ranged a thousand li collecting minerals, climbed every famed peak, sailed the sea, and sighed, "I could happily die like this."

sentences.zh: 」謝安嘗謂羲之曰：「中年以來，傷於哀樂，與親友別，輒作數日惡。

translations.literal: Xie An once told Xizhi, "Since middle years—harmed by sorrow and joy—with kin and friends parting—always several days ill.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An said, "Past forty grief and joy lay me low for days whenever friends leave."

sentences.zh: 」羲之曰：「年在桑榆，自然至此。

translations.literal: Xizhi said, "Years at sunset mulberry and elm—naturally arrive here.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi answered, "Twilight years naturally bring such fragility,

sentences.zh: 頃正賴絲竹陶寫，恆恐兒輩覺，損其歡樂之趣。

translations.literal: Recently just relying on silk and bamboo to mold expression—always fearing youngsters noticing—damaging their merry pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: So lately I lean on music for relief yet hide it from my children lest I spoil their cheer.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷以其誓苦，亦不復征之。

translations.literal: The court because his oath was bitter—also did not again summon him.
translations.idiomatic: The court, respecting his grim oath, ceased recalling him.

sentences.zh: 時劉惔為丹陽尹，許詢嘗就惔宿，床帷新麗，飲食豐甘。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Tan was Danyang Prefect—Xu Xun once approached Tan and lodged—bed curtains fresh and lovely—food and drink abundant and sweet.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tan governed Danyang when Xu Xun stayed over—fresh drapery, lavish fare.

sentences.zh: 詢曰：「若此保全，殊勝東山。

translations.literal: Xun said, "If thus preserved whole—especially surpasses Eastern Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "Safety like this beats hiding on Eastern Mountain."

sentences.zh: 」惔曰：「卿若知吉凶由人，吾安得保此。

translations.literal: Tan said, "Sir if you knew fortune and calamity lie with men—how could I preserve this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu replied, "If fate rested wholly in our hands I might stay so secure."

sentences.zh: 」羲之在坐，曰：「令巢許遇稷契，當無此言。

translations.literal: Xizhi sitting present said, "Supposing Chao and Xu met Ji and Xie—they ought not speak such words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi added, "Had hermits Chao and Xu served ministers Ji and Xie they would not talk so."

sentences.zh: 」二人並有愧色。

translations.literal: Both men together had ashamed expressions.
translations.idiomatic: Both men reddened.

sentences.zh: 初，羲之既優遊無事，與吏部郎謝萬書曰：

translations.literal: Initially—Xizhi already leisurely roaming without affairs—with Ministry of Personnel Gentleman Xie Wan wrote a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: While idle he wrote to Personnel Officer Xie Wan:

sentences.zh: 古之辭世者或被髮陽狂，或汙身穢跡，可謂艱矣。

translations.literal: Those of antiquity who quit the age—some disheveled hair feigned madness—some defiled body and filthy tracks—may be called arduous.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient recluses shaved their heads or played madmen—grim stratagems.

sentences.zh: 今僕坐而獲逸，遂其宿心，其為慶倖，豈非天賜！

translations.literal: Now your servant sitting obtains leisure—thereby fulfills long-held heart—its being fortunate—is this not Heaven's gift!
translations.idiomatic: I gain leisure without such theatrics—Heaven's gift!

sentences.zh: 違天不祥。

translations.literal: Violating Heaven is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Spurning Heaven invites ill luck.

sentences.zh: 頃東游還，修植桑果，今盛敷榮，率諸子，抱弱孫，游觀其間，有一味之甘，割而分之，以娛目前。

translations.literal: Recently returning from eastern roaming—planted mulberries and fruits—now lushly blooming—leading various sons—carrying weak grandsons—roaming viewing among them—having one flavor's sweetness—cutting and dividing it—to entertain before the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Home from an eastern tour I tended orchards now thick with fruit; I walk grandsons through the rows, split the sweetest morsels, and savor the moment.

sentences.zh: 雖植德無殊邈，猶欲教養子孫以敦厚退讓。

translations.literal: Although planting virtue not differing remote—still wishing to teach nurture sons and grandsons with honest generous yielding retreat.
translations.idiomatic: My virtue hardly matches sages, yet I drill the young in humility.

sentences.zh: 或以輕薄，庶令舉策數馬，仿佛萬石之風。

translations.literal: Some with light frivolousness—perhaps ordering raising whip counting horses—vaguely resembling Wan Shi's wind.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they seem flighty I hope they learn household reckoning like Shi Qing's sons.

sentences.zh: 君謂此何如？

translations.literal: Sir considers this how?
translations.idiomatic: What say you?

sentences.zh: 比當與安石東遊山海，並行田視地利，頤養閒暇。

translations.literal: Soon ought with Anshi roam eastern seas and mountains—and walk fields viewing land profit—nursing leisure quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xie An and I will wander coast and hill, inspect farms, and idle in peace.

sentences.zh: 衣食之餘，欲與親知時共歡宴，雖不能興言高詠，銜杯引滿，語田里所行，故以為撫掌之資，其為得意，可勝言邪！

translations.literal: Beyond clothing and food's surplus—wishing with kin and knowing ones sometimes jointly rejoice feasting—although unable to raise speech lofty chanting—holding cups drawing full—speaking fields and hamlets' doings—thereby taking as palm-slapping material—its being gratifying—can words exhaust it!
translations.idiomatic: After necessities I feast friends—maybe without lofty verse yet cups brimming, swapping village gossip—the pleasure cannot be told!

sentences.zh: 常依陸賈、班嗣、楊王孫之處世，甚欲希風數子，老夫志願盡於此也。

translations.literal: Constantly relying on Lu Jia, Ban Si, Yang Wangsun's conducting life—greatly wishing to aspire to those gentlemen's breeze—this old man's aspiration exhausts here.
translations.idiomatic: I model Lu Jia, Ban Si, Yang Wangsun—that finishes my ambition.

sentences.zh: 萬後為豫州都督，又遺萬書誡之曰：「以君邁往不屑之韻，而俯同群辟，誠難為意也。

translations.literal: Wan afterward became Area Commander of Yuzhou—again sent Wan a letter warning him saying, "With sir's lofty advancing disdainful rhythm—yet lowering to match the flock of ministers—indeed hard to suit the mind.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Wan commanded Yuzhou, Wang Xizhi warned him: "Your proud manner makes serving among petty officials galling,

sentences.zh: 然所謂通識，正自當隨事行藏，乃為遠耳。

translations.literal: Yet what is called comprehensive insight—just ought to follow affairs hide or show—thereby is far.
translations.idiomatic: True breadth means adapting—appear or withdraw as occasion demands.

sentences.zh: 願君每與士之下者同，則盡善矣。

translations.literal: I wish sir always join with gentlemen's lower ranks—then exhaustively good.
translations.idiomatic: Stay close to the rank and file—only then are you whole.

sentences.zh: 食不二味，居不重席，此復何有，而古人以為美談。

translations.literal: Eating no second flavor—dwelling not double mat—what again is here—yet ancients considered it fine conversation.
translations.idiomatic: Plain fare and a single mat cost nothing yet ancients praised such austerity.

sentences.zh: 濟否所由。

translations.literal: Relief or not—the means whereby.
translations.idiomatic: Success or collapse follows from that discipline.

sentences.zh: 實在積小以致高大，君其存之。

translations.literal: Truly lies in accumulating small thereby reaching tall and great—sir ought to preserve it.
translations.idiomatic: Greatness grows from small habits—remember this."

sentences.zh: 」萬不能用，果敗。

translations.literal: Wan could not use them—indeed was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Wan ignored every warning—and met ruin as predicted.

sentences.zh: 年五十九卒，贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At fifty-nine years he died; posthumously awarded Grand Master of Golden Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-nine and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 諸子遵父先旨，固讓不受。

translations.literal: The sons followed father's prior intent—firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His sons obeyed his wishes and steadfastly refused the posthumous rank.

sentences.zh: 子 凝之

translations.literal: Son—Ningzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Ningzhi.

sentences.zh: 有七子，知名者五人。

translations.literal: He had seven sons—those known were five.
translations.idiomatic: Of seven sons five became celebrated.

sentences.zh: 玄之早卒。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi died early.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Wang Xuanzhi, died young.

sentences.zh: 次凝之，亦工草隸，仕歷江州刺史、左將軍、會稽內史。

translations.literal: Next Ningzhi—also skilled in draft and clerical script—served successively as Inspector of Jiang Province, General of the Left, and interior minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Wang Ningzhi, himself adept at cursive and clerical hands, who rose to governor of Jiang, General of the Left, and interior minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 王氏世事張氏五斗米道，凝之彌篤。

translations.literal: The Wang clan for generations served the Zhang family's Five Pecks of Rice sect—Ningzhi devoted himself still more.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the Wangs followed Zhang Lu's Celestial Master sect; Wang Ningzhi observed it with fanatical zeal.

sentences.zh: 孫恩之攻會稽，僚佐請為之備。

translations.literal: When Sun En attacked Kuaiji—staff officers requested to prepare defenses for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun En stormed Kuaiji his aides begged to fortify the city.

sentences.zh: 凝之不從，方入靖室請禱，出語諸將佐曰：「吾已請大道，許鬼兵相助，賊自破矣。

translations.literal: Ningzhi did not comply—just entered the quiet chamber to pray—emerging told various command assistants, "I have already petitioned the Great Way—it promised ghost soldiers to aid us—the bandits will break of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ningzhi refused, closeted himself for Daoist prayer, then announced to his officers, "The Great Dao has pledged spirit troops—the rebels will collapse unaided.

sentences.zh: 」既不設備，遂為孫所害。

translations.literal: Having set no defenses—thereupon was killed by Sun.
translations.idiomatic: He posted no guards and Sun En slaughtered him.

sentences.zh: 子 徽之

translations.literal: Son—Huizhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Huizhi.

sentences.zh: 徽之字子猷。

translations.literal: Huizhi's courtesy name was Ziyou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huizhi, courtesy name Ziyou.

sentences.zh: 性卓犖不羈，為大司馬桓溫參軍，蓬首散帶，不綜府事。

translations.literal: By nature outstanding and unbridled—he became aide-de-camp to Grand Marshal Huan Wen—disheveled head and loose sash—not managing headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was brilliant and untamable on Grand Marshal Huan Wen's staff, hair tangled and belt dangling, ignoring paperwork.

sentences.zh: 又為車騎桓沖騎兵參軍，沖問：「卿署何曹？

translations.literal: Again he was cavalry aide to General of Chariots and Cavalry Huan Chong—Chong asked, "Sir, what bureau do you superintend?
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Huan Chong as cavalry adviser; Huan asked which office he headed.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「似是馬曹。

translations.literal: He replied, "Seems like the horse bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Probably the horses."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「管幾馬？

translations.literal: Again asked, "How many horses do you oversee?
translations.idiomatic: Huan pressed, "How many mounts?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不知馬，何由知數！

translations.literal: Said, "Not knowing horses—how by that know the count!
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I never learned horsemanship—how should I count them?"

sentences.zh: 」又問：「馬比死多少？

translations.literal: Again asked, "Of horses how many lately died?
translations.idiomatic: Huan asked how many had died recently.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「未知生，焉知死！

translations.literal: Said, "Not yet knowing life—how know death!
translations.idiomatic: He shot back, "I hardly grasp life—why discuss death?"

sentences.zh: 」嘗從沖行，值暴雨，徽之因下馬排入車中，謂曰：「公豈得獨擅一車！

translations.literal: Once following Chong on march—met violent rain—Huizhi thereupon dismounted, pushed aside attendants, entered the carriage, telling him, "Sir how can monopolize one carriage!
translations.idiomatic: Caught in a cloudburst with Huan Chong he shoved his way into the marshal's coach, demanding, "You cannot hog the dry seat alone."

sentences.zh: 」沖嘗謂徽之曰：「卿在府日久，比當相料理。

translations.literal: Chong once told Huizhi, "Sir in headquarters long—soon ought to arrange matters for you.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong later said, "You have loitered here forever—I should finally assign you real work."

sentences.zh: 」徽之初不酬答，直高視，以手版柱頰云：「西山朝來致有爽氣耳。」

translations.literal: Huizhi at first did not answer—only gazed high—using document tablet to prop cheek saying, "Western hills since dawn arrived with bracing air—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huizhi never replied—only stared skyward, chin on his writing board, and murmured, "The western peaks brought fresh morning air—that suffices."

sentences.zh: 時吳中一士大夫家有好竹，欲觀之，便出坐輿造竹下，諷嘯良久。

translations.literal: At the time a Wu gentleman-official's house had fine bamboo—wishing to view it—thereupon went out riding sedan chair arriving beneath bamboo—chanting and whistling long.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of fine bamboo at a Wu scholar's estate he rode straight there and whistled beneath the grove for ages.

sentences.zh: 主人灑掃請坐，徽之不顧。

translations.literal: The host sprinkled water sweeping inviting sit—Huizhi did not glance.
translations.idiomatic: The host swept a seat; Wang Huizhi ignored him.

sentences.zh: 將出，主人乃閉門，徽之便以此賞之，盡歎而去。

translations.literal: About to depart—the host then shut the gate—Huizhi with this appreciated him—fully sighed and left.
translations.idiomatic: As he turned to leave the owner slammed the gate—Wang Huizhi admired the snub and walked off sighing with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 嘗寄居空宅中，便令種竹。

translations.literal: Once lodging in an empty house—thereupon ordered bamboo planted.
translations.idiomatic: Renting an empty villa he immediately ordered bamboo planted.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，徽之但嘯詠，指竹曰：「何可一日無此君邪！

translations.literal: Someone asked the reason—Huizhi only whistled chanting—pointing at bamboo said, "How can one day lack this gentleman!
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he merely whistled and said of the plants, "A day without this gentleman is unthinkable!

sentences.zh: 」嘗居山陰，夜雪初霽，月色清朗，四望皓然，獨酌酒詠左思《招隱詩》，忽憶戴逵。

translations.literal: Once dwelling Shanyin—night snow just cleared—moonlight clear and bright—four views gleaming white—drinking alone wine chanting Zuo Si's 《Summons to Reclusion》—suddenly remembered Dai Kui.
translations.idiomatic: One snowy night in Shanyin, moonlight on fresh snow, he drank alone reciting Zuo Si's 《Summons to Reclusion》 and thought of Dai Kui.

sentences.zh: 逵時在剡，便夜乘小船詣之，經宿方至，造門不前而反。

translations.literal: Kui at the time was in Shan—thereupon night rode small boat going to him—after overnight only arrived—reaching gate did not advance but returned.
translations.idiomatic: Dai lived in Shan; Wang rowed through darkness till dawn, reached his gate, and turned home without knocking.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，徽之曰：「本乘興而行，興盡而反，何必見安道邪！

translations.literal: People asked the reason—Huizhi said, "Originally rode impulse to go—impulse exhausted then returned—why must see Andao!
translations.idiomatic: Asked to explain, he said, "I followed the mood; when the mood ended I left—why trouble Master Dao?"

sentences.zh: 」雅性放誕，好聲色，嘗夜與弟獻之共讀《高士傳贊》，獻之賞井丹高潔，徽之曰：「未若長卿慢世也。

translations.literal: By nature lofty and unrestrained—loving music and beauty—once night with younger brother Xianzhi jointly read 《Gaoshi zhuan zan》—Xianzhi admired Jing Dan's lofty purity—Huizhi said, "Not like Changqing's contempt for the age.
translations.idiomatic: He was wild and libertine, fond of pleasure. One night he and Wang Xianzhi read the 《Gaoshi zhuan zan》; Xianzhi praised Jing Dan's purity, but Huizhi preferred Sima Xiangru's contempt for convention.

sentences.zh: 」其傲達若此。

translations.literal: His arrogant openness thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his swaggering candor.

sentences.zh: 時人皆欽其才而穢其行。

translations.literal: People of the time all admired his talent yet reviled his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His age honored his genius yet despised his morals.

sentences.zh: 後為黃門侍郎，棄官東歸，與獻之俱病篤，時有術人云：「人命應終，而有生人樂代者，則死者可生。

translations.literal: Afterward became Gentleman at the Yellow Gate—abandoned office returning east—with Xianzhi both gravely ill—at the time a technician said, "When human fate should end—yet there is a living person glad to substitute—then the dead may live.
translations.idiomatic: As Palace Gate Gentleman he quit and went east; both brothers lay dying when a fortune-teller said, "If someone willingly trades years, the doomed may revive.

sentences.zh: 」徽之謂曰：「吾才位不如弟，請以餘年代之。

translations.literal: Huizhi told him, "My talent and rank do not match younger brother—please substitute with my surplus years.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huizhi said, "I am less gifted than my brother—take my leftover span for his.

sentences.zh: 」術者曰：「代死者，以己年有餘，得以足亡者耳。

translations.literal: The technician said, "Those substituting for the dead—because their own years have surplus—thereby can supply the deceased.
translations.idiomatic: The technician answered, "Substitution works only when one owns surplus life to give.

sentences.zh: 今君與弟算俱盡，何代也！

translations.literal: Now sir with younger brother reckon both exhausted—what substitution!
translations.idiomatic: Your allotments are empty—there is nothing to trade!

sentences.zh: 」未幾，獻之卒，徽之奔喪不哭，直上靈床坐，取獻之琴彈之，久而不調，歎曰：「嗚呼子敬，人琴俱亡！

translations.literal: Before long Xianzhi died—Huizhi rushed mourning—did not weep—straight ascended spirit couch sitting—took Xianzhi's zither playing it—long without tuning—sighed saying, "Alas Zijing—man and zither both perished!
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Xianzhi died. Wang Huizhi attended the wake dry-eyed, sat on the death couch, strummed his brother's zither, found it refuse to tune, and cried, "Dear Zijing—both man and instrument are gone!

sentences.zh: 」因頓絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon collapsed unconscious.
translations.idiomatic: He fainted on the spot.

sentences.zh: 先有背疾，遂潰裂，月餘亦卒。

translations.literal: Earlier had back ailment—thereupon ruptured open—over a month likewise died.
translations.idiomatic: An old spinal lesion reopened; within a month he too died.

sentences.zh: 子楨之。

translations.literal: Son Zhenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Zhenzhi.

sentences.zh: 徽之子 楨之

translations.literal: Huizhi's son—Zhenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huizhi's son Wang Zhenzhi.

sentences.zh: 楨之字公幹，歷位侍中、大司馬長史。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi's courtesy name was Gonggan—served successively as Palace Attendant and Chief Clerk to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhenzhi, courtesy name Gonggan, rose to palace attendant and chief clerk under the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 桓玄為太尉，朝臣畢集，問楨之：「我何如君亡叔？

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan was Grand Commandant—court ministers all assembled—asked Zhenzhi, "How do I compare with your late uncle?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Huan Xuan once asked him at court how he measured against the late Wang Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 」在坐咸為氣咽。

translations.literal: Those seated all for him held breath choked.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly froze.

sentences.zh: 楨之曰：「亡叔一時之標，公是千載之英。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi said his late uncle had been his generation's paragon while His Lordship was a hero for the ages.
