translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhenzhi answered that his uncle had topped his own age whereas Lord Huan topped the ages.

sentences.zh: 」一坐皆悅。

translations.literal: One seating all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The whole room relaxed.

sentences.zh: 子 操之

translations.literal: Son—Caozhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Caozhi.

sentences.zh: 操之字子重，曆侍中、尚書、豫章太守。

translations.literal: Caozhi's courtesy name was Zizhong—served as Palace Attendant, Minister, and Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Caozhi, courtesy name Zizhong, served as attendant, minister, and prefect of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 子 獻之

translations.literal: Son—Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 獻之字子敬。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's courtesy name was Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi, courtesy name Zijing.

sentences.zh: 少有盛名，而高邁不羈，雖閒居終日，容止不怠，風流為一時之冠。

translations.literal: From youth had great fame—yet lofty and unbridled—although idle dwelling whole days—bearing and deportment not slack—fengliu was crown of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Celebrated from boyhood, he was proud and free; even lounging all day his carriage never slackened, and his grace outshone everyone.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，嘗觀門生樗蒱，曰：「南風不競。

translations.literal: Years several—once watched disciples playing chupu—said, "The southern wind lacks vigor.
translations.idiomatic: Watching retainers gamble at chupu as a child he remarked, "The southern army lacks fight.

sentences.zh: 」門生曰：「此郎亦管中窺豹，時見一斑。

translations.literal: A disciple said, "This lad too peers through a tube at a leopard—sometimes glimpses one spot.
translations.idiomatic: A student retorted, "This boy squints through a bamboo tube—once in a while he spots a stripe.

sentences.zh: 」獻之怒曰：「遠慚荀奉倩，近愧劉真長。

translations.literal: Xianzhi angrily said, "Far I shame before Xun Fengqian—near I blush before Liu Zhenchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi flared, "Compared with Xun Can I fall short from afar; beside Liu Tan I feel ashamed up close.

sentences.zh: 」遂拂衣而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon brushed robe and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He swept out in a huff.

sentences.zh: 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安，二兄多言俗事，獻之寒溫而已。

translations.literal: Once with elder brothers Huizhi and Caozhi together visited Xie An—the two elder brothers much spoke vulgar affairs—Xianzhi only exchanged polite warmth.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Xie An with Wang Huizhi and Wang Caozhi, the elders prattled of trivia while Xianzhi offered only courteous small talk.

sentences.zh: 既出，客問安王氏兄弟優劣，安曰：「小者佳。

translations.literal: Already departed—guests asked An Wang clan brothers' superiority and inferiority—An said, "The youngest is fine.
translations.idiomatic: After they left someone asked which brother impressed him; Xie An named the youngest.

sentences.zh: 」客問其故，安曰：「吉人之辭寡，以其少言，故知之。

translations.literal: Guests asked the reason—An said, "The good man's speech is spare—because he seldom speaks—thereby know it.
translations.idiomatic: Guests pressed why, Xie said, "Virtuous men speak little—that reserve told me."

sentences.zh: 」嘗與徽之共在一室，忽然火發，徽之遽走，不遑取履。

translations.literal: Once with Huizhi sharing one chamber—suddenly fire broke out—Huizhi hurried fled—not leisurely taking sandals.
translations.idiomatic: Once fire erupted while he roomed with Wang Huizhi; the elder bolted barefoot.

sentences.zh: 獻之神色恬然，徐呼左右扶出。

translations.literal: Xianzhi spirit calm—slowly called attendants supporting him out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi stayed serene and let servants walk him out slowly.

sentences.zh: 夜臥齋中而有偷人入其室，盜物都盡。

translations.literal: Night lying in studio—yet there was thief entering his chamber—stolen goods entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves once stripped his bedroom while he slept.

sentences.zh: 獻之徐曰：「偷兒，氈青我家舊物，可特置之。

translations.literal: Xianzhi calmly said, "Thieves—the blue wool blanket is my family's heirloom—especially set it aside.
translations.idiomatic: He murmured, "Friends—the blue felt mat is an heirloom—kindly leave it.

sentences.zh: 」群偷驚走。

translations.literal: Band of thieves startled fled.
translations.idiomatic: They fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 工草隸，善丹青。

translations.literal: Skilled in draft and clerical script—good at cinnabar-green painting.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered cursive and clerical scripts and excelled at painting.

sentences.zh: 七八歲時學書，羲之密從後掣其筆不得，歎曰：「此兒後當復有大名。

translations.literal: Seven or eight years studying writing—Xizhi secretly from behind tugged his brush—not obtaining—sighed saying, "This child later ought again to have great name.
translations.idiomatic: At seven or eight Wang Xizhi tried snatching his brush from behind and could not—then sighed that the boy would earn a great name.

sentences.zh: 」嘗書壁為方丈大字，羲之甚以為能，觀者數百人。

translations.literal: Once wrote on wall one fathom square large characters—Xizhi greatly considered it capable—viewers several hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: He once brushed characters a yard tall on a wall; hundreds came to stare and his father praised the feat.

sentences.zh: 桓溫嘗使書扇，筆誤落，因畫作烏駁牸牛，甚妙。

translations.literal: Huan Wen once ordered him write fans—brush slipped dropping ink—thereupon painted motley cow—very marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen asked for fans Wang Xianzhi blotted the silk—then turned the slip into a splendid piebald cow.

sentences.zh: 起家州主簿、秘書郎，轉丞，以選尚新安公主。

translations.literal: Began office as prefectural chief clerk and palace secretary—transferred to assistant director—by selection married Princess of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as prefect recorder and palace secretary, rose to deputy director of the secretariat, and married the Princess of Xin'an by imperial selection.

sentences.zh: 嘗經吳郡，聞顧辟彊有名園。

translations.literal: Once passing Wu command—heard Gu Piqiang had a famous garden.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Wu he heard Gu Piqiang owned a celebrated estate.

sentences.zh: 先不相識，乘平肩輿徑入。

translations.literal: Earlier not acquainted—riding plain shoulder-litter went straight in.
translations.idiomatic: They had never met, yet Wang rode an open sedan straight onto the grounds.

sentences.zh: 時辟彊方集賓友，而獻之遊歷既畢，傍若無人。

translations.literal: At the time Piqiang just assembled guests and friends—yet Xianzhi touring finished—beside as if no others.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was entertaining guests; Wang toured the grounds as if alone.

sentences.zh: 辟彊勃然數之曰：「傲主人，非禮也。

translations.literal: Piqiang suddenly rebuked him saying, "Disrespecting host—not ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Gu exploded, "Insulting your host breaks propriety.

sentences.zh: 以貴驕士，非道也。

translations.literal: Using noble rank to bully gentlemen—not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Throwing princely rank at scholars violates the Way.

sentences.zh: 失是二者，不足齒之傖耳。

translations.literal: Losing these two—not worth mentioning vulgar bumpkins.
translations.idiomatic: Miss both marks and you are beneath contempt.

sentences.zh: 」便驅出門。

translations.literal: Then drove him out gate.
translations.idiomatic: He had Wang thrown out.

sentences.zh: 獻之傲如也，不以屑意。

translations.literal: Xianzhi arrogant as before—not regarding worth concern.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi stayed lordly and shrugged it off.

sentences.zh: 謝安甚欽愛之，請為長史。

translations.literal: Xie An greatly admired him—requested him as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An esteemed him and named him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 安進號衛將軍，復為長史。

translations.literal: An advanced title General Who Guards the Wei—again became Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie became General Who Guards the Wei Wang stayed chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 太元中，新起太極殿，安欲使獻之題榜，以為萬代寶，而難言之，試謂曰：「魏時陵雲殿榜未題，而匠者誤釘之，不可下，乃使韋仲將懸橙書之。

translations.literal: In Taiyuan era—newly raised Grand Ultimate Hall—An wished make Xianzhi write the plaque—considering it treasure for myriad generations—yet hard to speak—testing told him, "Wei times Lingyun Hall plaque not yet inscribed—yet craftsman mistakenly nailed it—unable to remove—thereupon made Wei Zhongjiang suspend on crate to write it.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiyuan, Xie wanted Wang to brush the new Taiji Hall plaque—a heirloom—but feared to command bluntly, so hinted with an old tale: Wei craftsmen once nailed the Lingyun plaque prematurely and forced minister Wei Zhongjiang to ink it while dangling from a scaffold.

sentences.zh: 比訖，須鬢盡白，裁餘氣息。

translations.literal: When finished—beard and temples all white—barely remaining breath.
translations.idiomatic: Wei descended white-haired and gasping.

sentences.zh: 還語子弟，宜絕此法。

translations.literal: Returning told sons and younger brothers—ought to cut off this method.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade his heirs ever to repeat such humiliation.

sentences.zh: 」獻之揣知其旨，正色曰：「仲將，魏之大臣，甯有此事！

translations.literal: Xianzhi guessed knowing his intent—solemn countenance said, "Zhongjiang—Wei great minister—could there be such matter!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi saw through the ploy and snapped, "Wei Zhongjiang was a Wei minister—that story is absurd!

sentences.zh: 使其若此，有以知魏德之不長。

translations.literal: Suppose it truly thus—thereby know Wei virtue's not long.
translations.idiomatic: Had it happened it would prove Wei lacked lasting virtue.

sentences.zh: 」安遂不之逼。

translations.literal: An thereupon did not force him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An dropped the subject.

sentences.zh: 安又問曰：「君書何如君家尊？

translations.literal: An again asked saying, "Sir's writing how compares with your honorable father?
translations.idiomatic: Xie later asked whether his calligraphy matched his father's.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「故當不同。

translations.literal: Replied saying, "Certainly ought differ.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "They should differ."

sentences.zh: 」安曰：「外論不爾。

translations.literal: An said, "Outside opinions not so.
translations.idiomatic: Xie said critics disagree.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「人那得知！

translations.literal: Replied saying, "People how can know!
translations.idiomatic: Wang replied, "How would outsiders know?"

sentences.zh: 」尋除建威將軍、吳興太守，徵拜中書令。

translations.literal: Shortly removed General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Wuxing—summoned honored Palace Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became General Who Establishes Might, prefect of Wuxing, then director of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，獻之遇疾，家人為上章，道家法應首過，問其有何得失。

translations.literal: Before long Xianzhi met illness—family for him submitted Daoist petition—Daoist law ought confess faults—asked him what gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Falling ill, his household filed a Daoist merit petition requiring confession of sins.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不覺餘事，惟憶與郗家離婚。

translations.literal: Replied saying, "Not aware of remaining matters—only remember divorcing the Xi family.
translations.idiomatic: He said he recalled nothing except divorcing Lady Xi.

sentences.zh: 」獻之前妻，郗曇女也。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's former wife—was Xi Tan's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: That wife had been Xi Tan's daughter.

sentences.zh: 俄而卒於官。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in post soon after.

sentences.zh: 安僖皇后立，以後父追贈侍中、特進、光祿大夫、太宰，諡曰憲。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Anxi was installed—because empress's father posthumously awarded Palace Attendant, Specially Advanced, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Mentor—posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wang became consort her father received posthumous ranks culminating in grand tutor with the epithet Xian.

sentences.zh: 無子，以兄子靜之嗣，位至義興太守。

translations.literal: Having no son—used elder brother's son Jingzhi as heir—rank reached Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he adopted his nephew Wang Jingzhi, who rose to prefect of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 時議者以為羲之草隸，江左中朝莫有及者，獻之骨力遠不及父，而頗有媚趣。

translations.literal: Critics of the time considered Xizhi's draft and clerical script—south of Yangzi and central court none matched him—Xianzhi's bone strength far did not reach father—yet somewhat had charming appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held Wang Xizhi's grass and clerical hands unrivaled south of the Yangzi; Wang Xianzhi lacked his father's structural power but showed seductive charm.

sentences.zh: 桓玄雅愛其父子書，各為一帙，置左右以玩之。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan by nature loved father and son's writing—each made one bundle—placed left and right to fondle them.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan treasured both men's works, keeping separate albums at hand.

sentences.zh: 始羲之所與共游者許邁。

translations.literal: Initially those Xizhi together roamed with—Xu Mai.
translations.idiomatic: Among Wang Xizhi's early companions was Xu Mai.

sentences.zh: 附 許邁

translations.literal: Attached—Xu Mai.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Xu Mai.

sentences.zh: 許邁，字叔玄，一名映，丹陽句容人也。

translations.literal: Xu Mai, courtesy name Shuxuan, another name Ying, was a man of Jurong in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mai, whose courtesy name was Shuxuan and who also took the name Ying, came from Jurong in Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世士族，而邁少恬靜，不慕仕進。

translations.literal: His house for generations was scholar-official clan—yet Mai in youth was tranquil and quiet—not aspiring to office pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Though born to a gentry family he remained placid as a youth and sought no career.

sentences.zh: 未弱冠，嘗造郭璞，璞為之筮，遇《泰》之《大畜》，其上六爻發。

translations.literal: Before capped adulthood—once visited Guo Pu—Pu for him divined—met Peace hexagram moving to Great Taming—the upper sixth line stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Before his capping he consulted Guo Pu, who cast yarrow stalks and drew Peace turning into Great Taming with the top line changing.

sentences.zh: 璞謂曰：「君元吉自天，宜學升遐之道。

translations.literal: Pu told him saying, "Lord—primordial auspiciousness from Heaven—ought study the way of ascending beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu said, "Heaven grants you supreme good fortune—you should pursue transcendence.

sentences.zh: 」時南海太守鮑靚隱跡潛遁，人莫之知。

translations.literal: " At the time Administrator of Nanhai Bao Jing concealed traces and vanished secretly—people none knew him.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Bao Jing, prefect of Nanhai, lived in hiding where no one could find him.

sentences.zh: 邁乃往候之，探其至要。

translations.literal: Mai thereupon went to await him—probed his utmost essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mai sought him out and drew out his deepest teachings.

sentences.zh: 父母尚存，未忍違親。

translations.literal: Father and mother still lived—not bearing to violate kin.
translations.idiomatic: His parents still lived, so he could not abandon them.

sentences.zh: 謂余杭懸霤山近延陵之茅山，是洞庭西門，潛通五嶽，陳安世、茅季偉常所遊處，於是立精舍於懸霤，而往來茅嶺之洞室，放絕世務，以尋仙館，朔望時節還家定省而已。

translations.literal: He said Yuhang's Xuansliu Mountain neared Yanling's Maoshan—was Dongting's western gate—secretly communicated with Five Marchmounts—Chen Anshi and Mao Jiwei's usual roaming places—thereupon erected a refined hut at Xuansliu—and traveled to Maoling's grotto chambers—rejecting worldly affairs—to seek immortal lodges—new and full moon seasons returning home to settle greeting only.
translations.idiomatic: He held that Xuansliu Mountain in Yuhang, near Maoshan at Yanling, formed the western portal of Dongting and linked to the Five Peaks—the haunt of adepts Chen Anshi and Mao Jiwei—so he built a hermitage there, shuttled to Maoshan's caves, cut worldly ties to pursue immortality, and came home only at each fortnight to visit his parents.

sentences.zh: 父母既終，乃遣婦孫氏還家，遂攜其同志遍游名山焉。

translations.literal: Father and mother having ended—thereupon sent wife Lady Sun returning home—thereupon carrying like-minded ones everywhere toured famous mountains.
translations.idiomatic: After they died he sent his wife the Lady Sun home and roamed sacred peaks with fellow seekers.

sentences.zh: 初采藥於桐廬縣之桓山，餌術涉三年，時欲斷穀。

translations.literal: Initially gathering herbs at Tonglu county's Huan Mountain—consumed atractylodes crossing three years—at times wished to cut grains.
translations.idiomatic: He first gathered drugs on Mount Huan in Tonglu, ate atractylodes for three years, and tried grain abstention.

sentences.zh: 以此山近人，不得專一，四面籓之，好道之徒欲相見者，登樓與語，以此為樂。

translations.literal: Because this mountain neared people—unable to obtain singleness—walled four sides—those fond of the Way wishing mutual viewing—ascended tower speaking with them—taking this as pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Because the peak stood too close to villages he fenced it on four sides; admirers who wished an audience spoke with him only from a lookout—a sport he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 常服氣，一氣千餘息。

translations.literal: Constantly ingesting qi—one breath over a thousand exhalations.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced breath retention until one cycle counted over a thousand counts.

sentences.zh: 永和二年，移入臨安西山，登岩茹芝，眇爾自得，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghe—moved into Lin'an western hills—climbing rocks eating fungus—dimly self-content—had intent to end there.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghe 2 he relocated to the western hills of Lin'an, climbing cliffs and chewing ganoderma in quiet contentment, resolved to die there.

sentences.zh: 乃改名玄，字遠遊。

translations.literal: Thereupon changed name to Xuan—courtesy name Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed himself Xuan with the courtesy name Yuanyou.

sentences.zh: 與婦書告別，又著詩十二首，論神仙之事焉。

translations.literal: With wife wrote farewell letter—again composed twelve poems—discoursing immortal matters.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his wife a parting letter and twelve poems on transcendence.

sentences.zh: 羲之造之，未嘗不彌日忘歸，相與為世外之交。

translations.literal: When Xizhi visited him—not once failing whole day forgetting return—mutually became beyond-the-world friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi's visits lasted whole days; they formed a friendship outside mundane life.

sentences.zh: 玄遺羲之書云：「自山陰南至臨安，多有金堂玉室，仙人芝草，左元放之徒，漢末諸得道者皆在焉。

translations.literal: Xuan sent Xizhi a letter saying, "From Shanyin south to Lin'an—many exist golden halls and jade chambers—immortals' mushroom herbs—Zuo Yuanfang's ilk—Han end various attained Dao ones all are there.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan wrote Wang Xizhi that south from Shanyin to Lin'an lay golden halls and jade chambers, immortal fungi, and masters like Zuo Ci—all the Han-era transcendents dwelt there.

sentences.zh: 」羲之自為之傳，述靈異之跡甚多，不可詳記。

translations.literal: Xizhi himself for him composed biography—narrating numinous traces extremely many—not able record in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi drafted his biography, crowded with marvels too numerous to list.

sentences.zh: 玄自後莫測所終，好道者皆謂之羽化矣。

translations.literal: Xuan from afterward none could fathom where he ended—those fond of Dao all called him feather transformed.
translations.idiomatic: None knew Xu Xuan's ultimate fate; Daoists declared him translated by feather wings.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：書契之興，肇乎中古，繩文鳥跡，不足可觀。

translations.literal: Appraisal says—writing tally's rise—began in middle antiquity—cord patterns and bird tracks—not sufficient worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: script arose in middle antiquity from knotted cords and bird traces hardly worth the eye.

sentences.zh: 末代去朴歸華，舒箋點翰，爭相跨尚，競其工拙。

translations.literal: Final ages departed plain returning splendor—spreading paper dotting brush—mutually striving to surpass esteem—competing their skill and clumsiness.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages forsook plain forms for ornament; brush danced across paper as rivals outdid one another in finesse.

sentences.zh: 伯英臨池之妙，無復餘蹤；

translations.literal: Boying beside pond's marvel—no again surplus traces;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhi's miracle by the ink-darkened pool leaves barely a trace;

sentences.zh: 師宜懸帳之奇，罕有遺跡。

translations.literal: Shi Yi's suspended curtain wonder—rarely has surviving marks.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yi's feat writing through a suspended curtain survives almost nowhere.

sentences.zh: 逮乎鐘王以降，略可言焉。

translations.literal: Down to Zhong and Wang—thereupon roughly may speak.
translations.idiomatic: Only from Zhong Yao and Wang Xizhi onward may one judge with confidence.

sentences.zh: 鐘雖擅美一時，亦為回絕，論其盡善，或有所疑。

translations.literal: Although Zhong monopolized beauty one generation—also turned aside utterly—discussing his exhaustive goodness—or exists doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao dominated his age yet belongs to a solitary pinnacle; whether even he reached flawless mastery invites debate.

sentences.zh: 至於布纖濃，分疏密，霞舒雲卷，無所間然。

translations.literal: As for spreading fine and thick—dividing sparse and dense—mist gathering dew knotting—appearance as if broken yet returning linked;
translations.idiomatic: His modulation of thick and thin, loose and tight—mist veiling, dew beading—looks broken yet flows unbroken;

sentences.zh: 但其體則古而不今，字則長而逾制，語其大量，以此為瑕。

translations.literal: yet his style then ancient and not present—characters then long and exceeding regulation—speaking his great measure—taking this as flaw.
translations.idiomatic: yet his manner feels archaic rather than modern and his glyphs run overlong against rule—that is his blemish.

sentences.zh: 獻之雖有父風，殊非新巧。

translations.literal: Xianzhi although having father's wind—utterly not new cleverness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi echoes his father yet lacks fresh ingenuity.

sentences.zh: 觀其字勢疏瘦，如隆冬之枯樹；

translations.literal: Observing his character momentum sparse lean—like deep winter's withered trees;
translations.idiomatic: His stroke momentum looks gaunt as leafless midwinter trees;

sentences.zh: 覽其筆蹤拘束，若嚴家之餓隸。

translations.literal: Perusing his brush traces constrained—like stern family's starving bondservant.
translations.idiomatic: his brush moves tight as starved house slaves under a harsh master.

sentences.zh: 其枯樹也，雖槎枿而無屈伸；

translations.literal: As for those withered trees—although stump sprouts yet without bending stretching;
translations.idiomatic: Those winter trees sprout snags yet never flex;

sentences.zh: 其餓隸也，則羈羸而不放縱。

translations.literal: as for those starving bondservants—then tethered lean without reckless release.
translations.idiomatic: those famished servants stay leashed and gaunt, never loose.

sentences.zh: 兼斯二者，故翰墨之病歙！

translations.literal: Combining these two—therefore brush ink's sickness collapses!
translations.idiomatic: Combine both faults and the ink itself grows sickly!

sentences.zh: 子雲近出，擅名江表，然僅得成書，無丈夫之氣，行行若縈春蚓，字字如綰秋蛇；

translations.literal: Ziyun recently emerged—monopolizing fame south of Yangzi—yet barely obtaining finished script—lacking great man's qi—line line as if tangled spring worms—character character as if knotted autumn snakes;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziyun lately rose to fame south of the river but masters only tidy copy—it lacks masculine vigor; each row coils like spring earthworms, each graph knots like autumn snakes;

sentences.zh: 臥王濛於紙中，坐徐偃於筆下；

translations.literal: laying Wang Meng within paper—seating Xu Yan beneath brush;
translations.idiomatic: it stretches Wang Meng supine on the page and seats Xu Yan rigid beneath the brush;

sentences.zh: 雖禿千兔之翰，聚無一毫之筋，窮萬谷之皮，斂無半分之骨；

translations.literal: although bald thousand rabbits' brushes—gather not one hair's sinew—exhaust myriad valleys' hides—collect not half fraction's bone;
translations.idiomatic: though it wears down a thousand rabbit brushes it gathers no fiber of tendon; though it stacks ten thousand valleys of hides it collects no splinter of bone;

sentences.zh: 以茲播美，非其濫名邪！

translations.literal: with this spreading beauty—is it not his undeserved reputation!
translations.idiomatic: to broadcast such work as virtue—is that not hollow fame?

sentences.zh: 此數子者，皆譽過其實。

translations.literal: These several gentlemen—all praise exceeds reality.
translations.idiomatic: These worthies are overrated one and all.

sentences.zh: 所以詳察古今，研精篆素，盡善盡美，其惟王逸少乎！

translations.literal: Therefore scrutinizing ancient and modern—studying essence of seal and plain—exhaustive good exhaustive beauty—perhaps only Wang Yishao!
translations.idiomatic: Survey past and present, refine seal and draft script, and find perfection solely in Wang Xizhi!

sentences.zh: 觀其點曳之工，裁成之妙，煙霏露結，狀若斷而還連；

translations.literal: Observing his dotting and dragging's craft—tailoring completion's marvel—mist flying dew binding—appearance as if cut yet returning linked;
translations.idiomatic: Study his dots and sweeps, his shaped compositions—mist and dew interwoven—seeming severed yet endlessly linked;

sentences.zh: 鳳翥龍蟠，勢如斜而反直。

translations.literal: phoenix soaring dragon coiling—momentum as if slanting yet contrary straight.
translations.idiomatic: phoenix lifting, dragon curling—energy seems slanted yet resolves upright.

sentences.zh: 玩之不覺為倦，覽之莫識其端，心慕手追，此人而已。

translations.literal: Playing it—unknowingly never wearying—viewing it—none discerns its tip—heart admiring hand chasing—this person alone.
translations.idiomatic: One handles his work without tiring, gazes without finding its limit—only he draws mind and hand together.

sentences.zh: 其餘區區之類，何足論哉！

translations.literal: The remaining petty sorts—how worth discussing!
translations.idiomatic: The lesser scribblers scarcely merit mention!
